//name: The extension ID is publisher.name, so this reads `ffwf.tau-runtime`. It is a SEPARATE extension from `ffwf.tau-code` and not a dependency of it: see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 14.2 for why optional means `getExtension` at runtime rather than `extensionDependencies`, which is mandatory and auto-installs.
name: tau-runtime
//displayName: Sits next to `tau code` in the extension list, which is the whole point of the name: a user looking at what they installed can see that the runtime is a second thing they can remove.
description: A self-contained CPython with tau installed into it, for the tau code extension. Optional: tau code uses a system tau when this is absent.
//tauSpec: Which tau is installed into the shipped interpreter. ONE copy of this number: scripts/build-payload.mjs reads it from here, and the payload's manifest.json records what pip ACTUALLY installed by reading the dist-info back, so the pin and the artifact cannot drift into disagreeing quietly. 0.10.1 is protocol 1.5 -- the same release the container pins and the same one packages/protocol/src/generated.ts was generated from. Bump it with the Dockerfile's TAU_SPEC, not on its own: two artifacts shipping two taus is how a client ends up tested against neither. The `[tui]` extra is deliberately absent -- rpc_mode.py imports tau_agent_core.rpc and tau_coding_agent.headless, neither of which touches Textual, and tau's own pyproject measures the difference at 15 packages / 13 MB against 27 / 31 MB.
//extensionKind: `workspace`, matching ffwf.tau-code. The runtime is spawned wherever the agent runs -- over SSH, in WSL, in a devcontainer -- so a runtime that installed on the laptop while tau ran on the remote would be the wrong architecture's binaries in the wrong place. VS Code's platform-specific resolution downloads the build matching the REMOTE host, which is the one this has to be.
//capabilities: A payload of files this extension ships, spawned by another extension. It reads nothing from the workspace, so trust does not gate it; it is real files on a real disk, so a virtual workspace has nowhere to put it.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The runtime is a directory of real files that has to be executed, and a virtual workspace has no filesystem to execute it from.

scripts.//package: --no-dependencies for the same reason ffwf.tau-code passes it: esbuild bundles the entry, and vsce would otherwise walk the workspace-hoisted ../../node_modules. --target is NOT optional here -- a runtime VSIX with no target claims to run everywhere and ships one platform's binaries.
